title: The Evening Brief: Extreme fear grips markets; whales accumulate bitcoin
dek: Bitcoin slid 2.29% on Tuesday as the Fear and Greed Index hit 11, its extreme level, while institutional flows showed $356.7 million in bitcoin moving off exchanges. Major coins posted steep declines across the board, with spot Bitcoin ETFs taking in $4.0 million on the day.
author: GoCheckMyCrypto
key_fact: Markets entered extreme capitulation territory on Tuesday, marked by oversold technicals and persistent selling pressure, yet whale accumulation into self-custody and modest ETF inflows suggest institutional participants are differentiating between panic and opportunity.
bottom_line: Bitcoin dropped 2.29% on Tuesday as the Fear and Greed Index hit extreme 11, marking capitulation conditions on the technical boards, yet whale accumulation into self-custody and modest spot Bitcoin ETF inflows on the day signal institutional differentiation between panic and bottom formation. The desk's boards show severely oversold RSI readings, golden crosses still in place, and persistent stablecoin inflows to exchanges, while Bitcoin whale outflows totaled $356.7 million off exchanges. Wednesday's PCE report and the Bitcoin difficulty adjustment (estimated +8.94%, 643 blocks to go) are the week's key checkpoints.
body: Crypto markets deepened their retreat on Tuesday as panic selling intensified across major assets. Bitcoin fell 2.29% over 24 hours, extending its decline to down 5.57% over seven days and down 24.23% over thirty days. Ether posted similar pressure: down 1.93% on the day, down 6.05% over seven days, and down 27.47% over thirty days. Solana dropped 2.80% on the day while holding slight gains of up 0.66% over the week. Smaller caps showed sharper moves: Dogecoin down 1.59% on the day, Cardano down 1.87% on the day, and XRP down 1.55% on the day. The desk's Fear and Greed Index registered 11, its extreme reading, marking the most acute panic level in the last 30 days (which ranged from 10 to 51).

Technical positioning shows widespread capitulation signals. Per the desk's boards, Bitcoin's RSI14 sits at 25.1, Ether's at 28.2, and Solana's at 29.3, all severely oversold readings. Bitcoin trades 51.9% below its 12-month high of $124,739.81, Ether 64.1% below $4,690.84, and Solana 70.0% below $232.63. Despite these lows, golden crosses remain in place across Bitcoin, Ether, Solana, and BNB, a potential indicator of longer-term reversal structure. Volatility has spiked: Bitcoin's 30-day realized volatility stands at 47.5%, Ether at 66.4%, and Solana at 65.1%.

Institutional flows paint a more nuanced picture. The desk's Whale Watch board shows $410.9 million in net value moving off exchanges over the past 24 hours, driven by $356.7 million in bitcoin leaving exchanges and $54.3 million in ethereum exiting as well. The largest single move was $268.5 million in bitcoin withdrawn from Coinbase Institutional. This follows weeks of sustained outflows: the week ending November 21 saw $1,615 million move off exchanges, the week ending November 14 saw $1,551 million move off exchanges, and the week ending November 7 saw $4,125 million move off exchanges. At the same time, stablecoins moved in the opposite direction: $45.7 million in net stablecoin inflows to exchanges over the past 24 hours, with $169.4 million in USDT deposited to Binance and $124.9 million to Bitfinex offsetting smaller outflows.

Spot Bitcoin ETFs took in $4.0 million on the day, November 24, though the week through November 24 shows spot Bitcoin ETFs saw net outflows of $2,123.7M over the week, a signal of persistent institutional redemptions over the five-session window. Per the desk's leverage boards, funding rates remain calm: Bitcoin at 0.65% annualized at OKX, Ether at 0.85% annualized. Long-to-short ratios remain tilted toward longs across all major assets, Bitcoin at 2.61, Ether at 3.0, Solana at 2.86, suggesting leveraged shorts are not building despite the selloff. Liquidations over the past 3 to 10 hours favor short sellers: Bitcoin saw $868,076 in long liquidations versus $89,645 in shorts; Ether saw $607,235 in longs versus $39,336 in shorts.

The calendar ahead shapes the week's focus. Wednesday, November 25, brings the Personal Income and Outlays (PCE) release, the week's primary macro data point. The desk's calendar notes the Bitcoin difficulty adjustment, estimated at +8.94%, arrives with 643 blocks remaining.
